globalSetup: Build and package Y Space with Node 24 from the implementation worktree.
Load .env.pipedream without printing values or enabling shell tracing.
Prepare a local HTTP/HTTPS cookie fixture with a unique secret sentinel and cookies covering persistent, session, HttpOnly, Secure/SameSite, expired, malformed, prefix, and partitioned cases.
Install the unpacked Y Space Cookie Import extension in Chrome and Brave using separate labeled profiles.
Authenticate Codex and OpenCode; complete Claude Code login interactively without recording credentials.
Open renderer DevTools, retain application logs, and record provider-generated MCP configuration in a redacted test-only capture.
Before each test, record the exact app build commit, provider version, model ID, and relevant persisted-state checksum without reading secret values.

tests.title: Y Space identity and compatibility migration
tests.userStory: As an existing Lightcode user, I see Y Space everywhere while my prior work and browser session remain intact.
setupInstrumentation: Seed one project, thread, custom MCP named chrome, browser tab, and persistent test cookie in the pre-migration app.
Capture before-state IDs and non-secret counts.
steps: Launch the packaged Y Space build over the seeded profile.
Inspect the title bar, sidebar, composer, settings, skills, plugins, dialogs, and About/update surfaces.
Open the seeded project/thread/tab and invoke the user custom MCP named chrome.
expectedResults: All visible owned branding says Y Space.
Seeded data and browser state remain available.
No external Chrome built-in appears, while the user custom MCP still works.

tests.title: Manual embedded multi-tab lifecycle
tests.userStory: As a user, I can work with several independent embedded pages like regular browser tabs.
setupInstrumentation: Launch with an empty embedded browser panel.
Enable screenshot capture and browser event recording.
steps: Create three tabs and navigate each to a distinct local fixture route.
Confirm each page assigns a distinct tab title, then reorder, refresh, switch among, and close the middle tab.
Quit and relaunch Y Space.
expectedResults: Each tab retains independent URL/history/page state.
The remaining order and selected tab are correct.
Supported persistent tab state is restored after relaunch.

tests.title: Codex controls and reuses embedded tabs
tests.userStory: As a Codex user, I can ask the agent to find an existing tab or open a new one and test the page.
setupInstrumentation: Pre-open two fixture tabs with distinguishable titles and URLs.
Start a Codex GUI task using gpt-5.6-luna.
steps: Ask Codex for an overview of all tabs.
Ask it to find and activate one existing tab by partial title, click/type through a form, and capture a screenshot.
Ask it to open-or-focus a URL already present, then open a genuinely new URL and close it.
expectedResults: The overview exactly matches visible embedded tabs.
The existing tab is reused rather than duplicated.
Interactions and evidence occur only inside the embedded browser and the tab group carries the exact task identity.
proofToCapture: Exact task identity returned by app controls.

tests.title: Claude Code terminal and GUI browser access
tests.userStory: As a Claude Code user, Browser and app controls work by default in both supported presentation modes.
setupInstrumentation: Complete Claude Code login interactively.
Record the live Claude model ID selected for each run.
steps: Start a terminal-mode task without mentioning Browser and list available tabs/tools.
Navigate and verify a fixture workflow, then resume it.
Repeat in GUI mode with another available Claude model or effort setting.
expectedResults: Both modes receive launch-scoped embedded Browser and app-controls MCPs by default.
Resume preserves task/tab identity.
No external-browser tool or permission is present.

tests.title: Concurrent OpenCode GUI identity isolation
tests.userStory: As an OpenCode user, concurrent tasks in one project control their own tab groups without identity collisions.
setupInstrumentation: Use OpenCode 1.18.23 or newer.
Start two GUI tasks in the same directory using opencode/gpt-5.6-luna and zai/glm-4.5-flash.
steps: In parallel, ask each task to create a differently titled tab and report its current task.
Have each task activate and inspect only its tab.
Close one task and attempt a tool call using its stale provider session, then continue with the live task.
expectedResults: Each tab is owned by the correct exact task and no configuration overwrites the other.
Forged/model-provided identity is ignored.
The stale session fails closed while the live session remains functional.
proofToCapture: Two task transcripts with model IDs.

tests.title: Global Browser hard-disable and core skills
tests.userStory: As an administrator, I can disable Browser globally; otherwise every provider gets the Y Space core skills without installation.
setupInstrumentation: Prepare fresh Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode tasks.
Record effective MCP/skill inventories.
steps: Verify both Y Space core skills and Browser are present by default for all providers.
Disable Browser globally and start fresh tasks for each provider.
Re-enable Browser and start one final task.
expectedResults: Core skills require no plugin installation and a user-owned collision is not overwritten.
The hard-disable removes Browser from all fresh launches without removing app controls.
Re-enabling restores Browser.

tests.title: Pair two cookie-import sources
tests.userStory: As a user, I can pair Chrome and Brave profiles as cookie sources without granting browser control.
setupInstrumentation: Install the unpacked extension in Chrome and Brave.
Inspect extension manifest permissions and retain bridge logs with values redacted.
steps: Begin pairing in Y Space and enter the expiring code in Chrome.
Repeat with a distinct Brave source label.
Disconnect/reconnect both, forget one source, and verify its old token cannot reconnect.
expectedResults: Both sources can coexist and show only redacted metadata.
Only cookie/storage/alarms plus exact optional host permissions are requested.
Revocation is immediate and no plaintext token is persisted by Y Space.
proofToCapture: Hashed-pairing persisted-state inspection and revoked reconnect failure.

tests.title: Preview, confirm, and use imported authentication
tests.userStory: As a user, I can preview cookie counts, explicitly approve an import, and use the authenticated session in every embedded tab and agent.
setupInstrumentation: Authenticate the Chrome fixture with the sentinel cookies.
Open the same unauthenticated origin in an embedded tab.
steps: Request import for the exact active origin and approve temporary permission in the extension.
Verify preview shows domain/count/unsupported metadata only and confirm selected domains in Y Space.
Reload the embedded page, open a second embedded tab, and ask Codex to verify the authenticated UI.
Capture /cookie-status and /account/cookie-status in the source and embedded browsers; verify the value-free presence rows for persistent, session, path, prefix, expired, and partitioned cases.
Quit/relaunch, capture both status pages again, and verify persistent cookies remain while the session cookie is absent.
expectedResults: No values cross during preview.
Commit writes only validated in-scope cookies and flushes the embedded partition.
Both embedded tabs and the agent can use the authenticated UI; persistence behavior matches cookie type.
The partitioned and expired rows stay absent in Y Space, the path-scoped row appears only under /account, and no status response contains the sentinel.
proofToCapture: Value-free root/account cookie-status captures before import, after import, and after restart.
Redacted import counts and restart results.

tests.title: Cookie-import denial, limits, and legacy-protocol rejection
tests.userStory: As a security-conscious user, denied or malformed imports fail safely and the extension cannot control any browser tab.
setupInstrumentation: Prepare denial, oversized, malformed, out-of-scope, expired, partitioned, and secret-sentinel fixtures.
Monitor app logs, renderer IPC/events, persistence, telemetry, and browser activity.
steps: Deny origin permission, retry, then cancel before commit.
Attempt more than 750 cookies and more than 4 MiB, then a mixed invalid set.
Send legacy listTabs, attach, openTab, and CDP messages.
Search all monitored surfaces for the sentinel.
expectedResults: Denied/cancelled flows write nothing and release permissions.
Oversized sets fail without truncation; invalid items produce redacted counts/partial status.
Every legacy control message closes the bridge and no external tab changes.
The sentinel appears only in the source browser cookie store and embedded Electron cookie store.
proofToCapture: External tabs before/after video or screenshots.

tests.title: Personal Pipedream MCP OAuth
tests.userStory: As a user, I can enable Pipedream Personal MCP, authenticate, and use a harmless read-only integration action from each agent.
setupInstrumentation: Use a non-production Pipedream account and harmless connected app.
Record MCP server/tool inventory before authorization.
steps: Enable Personal MCP and complete OAuth in the newly opened embedded Y Space browser tab.
From fresh Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode tasks, inspect pd tools and perform one read-only action.
Sign out in Y Space and retry from a fresh task.
expectedResults: Managed server pd appears only after enable/auth and works in all providers.
Each real action reaches Pipedream and returns the expected account-scoped data.
Sign-out removes Y Space authorization without deleting Pipedream app/account connections.

tests.title: BYO Pipedream Connect account and provider exposure
tests.userStory: As a developer, I can use environment-managed Pipedream Connect credentials to connect an app and grant agents deterministic access.
setupInstrumentation: Load the four Pipedream variables with shell tracing disabled.
Use a disposable or harmless app account and record Pipedream accounts before the test.
steps: Open Connections and probe the configured project.
Search the app catalog, launch Connect, authorize an account, and enable agent access.
Start Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode tasks; list integrations and execute one read-only action through the app-specific MCP.
expectedResults: UI says environment-managed and exposes no credential values.
A real Pipedream account appears for the stable Y Space external user.
All providers receive only loopback URL/local bearer and reach the same selected account.
proofToCapture: Redacted provider configs and three tool traces.

tests.title: Pipedream access disable, disconnect, and restart cleanup
tests.userStory: As a user, I can revoke agent access or disconnect an account and know old routes no longer work.
setupInstrumentation: Begin with one healthy enabled BYO account and capture its redacted managed server name/route fingerprint.
Record Pipedream account state.
steps: Disable agent access and reload/relaunch each provider.
Re-enable access, verify it returns, then disconnect with confirmation.
Call the old relay route and restart Y Space.
expectedResults: Disabled access removes the managed MCP without deleting the upstream account.
Disconnect removes the real Pipedream account and immediately invalidates the old route.
Restart reconciles to disconnected state with no stale tool exposure.

tests.title: Pipedream relay spoofing and consequential retry safety
tests.userStory: As a user, one integration cannot impersonate another or duplicate a consequential action during reauthentication.
setupInstrumentation: Use two disposable app bindings and an upstream test double or observable harmless action.
Capture request counts and redacted headers at the controlled boundary.
steps: Send bad bearer, Host, Origin, route, spoofed Authorization, and spoofed x-pd headers.
Try one binding's MCP session ID on the other binding.
Force a 401 during a tools/call and during a read-only handshake.
expectedResults: Untrusted requests fail locally and spoofed headers never reach upstream.
Sessions cannot cross bindings.
Consequential tools/call executes at most once; only safe handshake/read behavior may retry after token refresh.

tests.title: Secret inheritance and persistence audit
tests.userStory: As a user, cookie and Pipedream secrets are usable where required but never leak to agents or durable diagnostics.
setupInstrumentation: Use unique cookie and Pipedream sentinel values.
Prepare a test-only process-env probe inside each provider and read-only scans of allowed Y Space state paths.
steps: Start all three providers and check for PIPEDREAM_* variables without printing any value.
Exercise cookie import and Pipedream actions.
Scan logs, renderer DevTools, provider configs, settings, SQLite, telemetry, crash context, and temporary files for sentinel hashes/values.
expectedResults: No provider inherits any PIPEDREAM_* variable.
No secret/token/cookie value crosses renderer IPC or appears in durable/diagnostic surfaces.
Only approved encrypted credential state, token hashes, and Electron cookies contain the necessary secret material.
proofToCapture: Negative sentinel scan report with paths covered.
Encrypted-state and file-mode evidence without values.
